A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Context Tuning and retain matching methods, benchmarks and principal results. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated qualitative examples.

before.justification: V2 reports original benchmark accuracies, training times, ablations, memory measurements and diagnostic experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds BBH experiments varying demonstration counts and training duration in Appendices G and H.

M1.justification: CT-Prompt, CT-KV, masking, Token Dropout, TTT+CT-KV and the Appendix D variants retain their algorithmic steps and objectives. Clarified masking implementation and revised noise specification do not establish a procedural redesign.

E1.justification: The four benchmark families remain, and the added BBH studies vary counts and subsets within existing coverage. However, Section 5.1 changes BBH's description from 27 tasks across 23 task types to 23 tasks without identifying task membership. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects regrouping, a correction or actual task removal.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in matched experiments. LoRA, Rank-Stabilized LoRA and DoRA already appear in v2 Table 1 and remain in v3, alongside the same ICL, prompt/prefix tuning and TTT baselines. The new BBH studies reuse existing comparators.

E3.justification: V3 adds 25/50/100-shot BBH evaluation on eight tasks whose prompts fit an 8K-token window, using Llama 3-8B-Instruct and 3–60 training epochs, plus a separate 4–64-epoch stability sweep. The demonstration-retrieval evaluation is removed. Existing metrics and tabulated learning-rate/iteration choices remain; Appendix D's written noise specification is revised without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: The supplementary analysis package changes substantially: v3 adds BBH many-shot and extended-training studies, while removing v2 Section 5.9's demonstration-retrieval diagnostic and Table 4's ARC solved-task overlap analysis. Existing design ablations, corruption tests, initialization studies and memory profiling remain. The ARC qualitative examples are retained through relocation and splitting.

E5.justification: V3 Table 3 explicitly exempts ARC from its five-seed statement, correcting the earlier unqualified caption to reflect fixed demonstrations. Existing mean/standard-deviation reporting is retained, with no stated increase in runs. New Tables 11–12 provide point accuracies without additional run-count or uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Principal benchmark scores and retained appendix results are unchanged apart from equivalent rounding. New Table 11 reports 62.6% for CT-KV at 100-shot/40 epochs versus 46.5% for ICL; Table 12 reports CT-KV staying near 57.9% through 64 epochs while Prefix Tuning declines after its peak. V2's ARC overlap counts (44, 51, 9, 296) and retrieval accuracies (81.9%, 84.1%, 89.3%, 22.6%) disappear, substantially changing the supplementary results.

T1.justification: Appendix D changes the stated CT-Prefix perturbation law from N(0, 0.02) to the explicit vector Gaussian N(0, 0.02^2 I). This is a limited formal specification revision; the optimization equations, Fisher calculation and asymptotic complexity results retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain demonstration-initialized context optimization, CT-KV's efficiency relative to CT-Prompt and TTT, and complementarity with TTT. V3's abstract foregrounds memory refinement and superiority to ICL, but these ideas and claims were already present in v2.

C2.justification: V3 removes the retrieval-error-based explanation of insufficient KV encoding and adds an interpretation attributing extended-training stability to masking and dropout. The ARC overfitting limitation and grid-shape-bias explanation remain in Appendix J. The word-sorting explanation is corrected from comparing second letters to comparing later letters.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 now specifies setting masked attention positions to zero, and Appendix D explicitly specifies Gaussian covariance. The new BBH studies document their model, context-window restriction and training sweeps. Existing hardware, optimizer, hyperparameter tables and project access link are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds Agarwal et al. on many-shot learning and meta-prompt-learning references by Pan, Huang and Qin. It also describes Deutch et al. as challenging, rather than supporting, the implicit-gradient-descent interpretation. Most other reference changes update metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten around memory refinement, the body receives copyediting, and acknowledgments change. Section 5.9 is removed and qualitative discussion is reorganized between Section 5.8 and the appendices, while most method and experimental prose retains its structure.

P2.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the displays: it removes two diagnostic tables, adds two BBH tables, splits v2's two-panel ARC Figure 6 between the main text and appendix, and moves the failure comparison to Appendix J. Tables are resized/reformatted, running headers and decorative rules are removed, and section styling changes throughout. The relocated examples are not new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The new BBH sweeps provide useful evidence about higher demonstration counts and prolonged optimization, and clearer technical specifications modestly improve reproducibility. These gains are partly offset by removing the ARC regression counts and retrieval diagnostic, while the new tables lack uncertainty details. The principal benchmark evidence and explicit ARC failure examples remain, supporting a limited overall improvement.
